svg.title: Reconfigurable Hankel cell: shared DFG pair and cross-SFG weight-increment output
svg.desc: Cleaned functional schematic based on the user-authored simplified_hankel_multiplier.svg. One shared pair of DFG sections computes forward and adjoint operations with exchanged pump assignments. Forward input u=x uses old adaptive W then fixed M; adjoint input u=e uses M then the same old W. DFG(p,u)=H(p)conjugate(u); the temporal sum has normalization c=1/128. Data modes A and B are distinguishable bands, polarizations or spatial modes near 1550 nm; P denotes the coefficient/pump band near 775 nm. Pump muxes combine P with data; the writer mux combines A and B with the mode selection needed for cross-SFG. The first DFG filter retains 64 B lines and rejects residual pumps before the writer; the second retains 64 A lines. The SFG filter retains all 127 P coefficient lines and no temporal summation is applied to the writer. In backward mode, the router/splitter feeds r_m=H(M_m)conjugate(e) to DFG2 and the SFG writer using a calibrated split, or selects separate timed visits. The writer also receives saved forward x, and produces a calibrated weight increment Delta W = eta*c times the full frequency-index convolution x*r_m. The write amplitude/phase MZI sets the complex scale of the increment. Coherent addition to the matching old W, retention and recirculating-loop gain are external to this Hankel cell and shown in Figure 1b. This figure supplies the arithmetic and weight-increment interfaces, not the detailed timing or memory circuitry. Input/error holds, pump swapping hardware, old-state access, write windows and guard intervals are reserved for the subsequent timing panel. Shared-accumulator visits must respect valid-window spacing. Three spiral motifs abbreviate seven stages and 128 taps; they are not three physical stages. Selected-port losses, conversion phases, router tap factors, cross-SFG isolation, amplifier technology and broad-band calibration remain implementation requirements. Geometry is not a fabrication layout. DejaVu Sans text remains editable. Pale-gray cladding, signal-colored cores, purple DFG, teal SFG, amber filters, rose gain symbols and gold electrical controls follow the source library. No background rectangle. Propagation arrows, component labels and the mode/band key occupy separate Inkscape layers. Signal gradients identify W (purple), M (amber), x (blue), error e (red), forward output y (cyan), adjoint output g_x (magenta), first-DFG intermediate (violet-blue) and Delta W (teal). Paired input, pump and read-output gradients denote forward/adjoint alternatives, not a physical color or time dependence. Mode-specific active routes are shown separately in Figure 1b. Ideal unselected pump/data mux output ports contain cladding but no drawn core. Both intermediate-router outputs are present because this panel defines the functional cell across operating modes. Gradients are native editable SVG.
